The failing test `testUnionOfVariableAndNode` in the class `VariableTest` of the `org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.compiler` package appears to be invoking `JXPathContext.iteratePointers` with the XPath expression "$var | /MAIN/A" to iterate over pointers related to a variable and nodes in the XML document.

The current bug report states that an exception is being thrown with the message "Cannot compare pointers that do not belong to the same tree". This suggests that there is an issue with comparing pointers from different trees within the JXPath library.

By looking at the code snippets of relevant methods in the `JXPathContext` class:
1. The `newContext(Object contextBean)` method is used to create a new `JXPathContext` with the specified context bean.
2. The `getVariables()` method retrieves the `Variables` object associated with the `JXPathContext`.

Based on the behavior described in the failing test and the exception message in the bug report, it seems that the expression "$var | /MAIN/A" is attempting to combine pointers related to the variable "var" with pointers to nodes in the XML document. This combination is causing the exception related to comparing pointers from different trees.

To diagnose the issue further, we need to understand how variables and nodes are handled in the `iteratePointers` method and why comparing pointers from different trees is leading to this exception. We may need to inspect the implementation of the `iteratePointers` method in the `JXPathContext` class to see how it processes the specified XPath expression and handles the combination of variable and node pointers.

Shall we proceed to obtain the code snippet of the `iteratePointers` method to investigate the issue further?

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
